headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: oh-my-openagent’s broad networked toolchain can ingest and act on content while awesome-nlp provides no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent exposes runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and browser/tool surfaces, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction path. awesome-nlp is a non-runnable list with no isolation or parser controls, so the pairwise bridge is indirect but plausible. No shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent ingests content from a shared file, MCP server, or browser page as instructions
IF awesome-nlp content is copied into an agent prompt without sanitization
mitigations: Disable browser/MCP tool use for untrusted content during the session
Require explicit provenance tags before treating file or web text as instructions
Use a read-only workspace for any copied content
requires-engineering: add instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: oh-my-openagent touches session history, project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, and provider auth data, and has broad network egress. awesome-nlp itself has no runtime surfaces, but if it is paired in the same workspace, sensitive local files can flow into oh-my-openagent and then out via APIs. The leakage path is plausible in default agent workflows.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or copied files
IF oh-my-openagent is allowed to send retrieved context to external APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Turn off external API calls for the session
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Review and redact AGENTS.md and auth prompts before use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write surfaces, but oh-my-openagent can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and write to multiple config/file locations. If both are pointed at the same installation or repo, oh-my-openagent can overwrite or race on shared files while awesome-nlp offers no locking. The conflict is real but narrower than unrestricted same-dir writes.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or config directory
IF multiple oh-my-openagent instances run against one installation
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Avoid concurrent runs against the same install
Back up config files before editing
Use file locks for shared mutable paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can use team messaging, browser, and API tools, so if it treats upstream content as authoritative it can turn a bad suggestion into external actions. awesome-nlp is a static resource, but when its contents are surfaced through the pair, oh-my-openagent may operationalize them without verification. That makes the downstream blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent uses copied content or retrieved text as facts without verification
IF team_send_message or task creation is enabled for the session
mitigations: Require human review before sending messages or creating tasks
Add a verification step for any facts imported from external content
Disable team_* actions for untrusted sessions
Log source provenance alongside every action
requires-engineering: enforce action gating on unverified inputs

E_compliance.rationale: oh-my-openagent explicitly handles provider auth prompts, session history, and anonymous telemetry, while awesome-nlp is a static open-source list with no runtime compliance surface. The pair creates a mismatch if regulated or sensitive data is entered into oh-my-openagent and then retained or transmitted under its broader networked defaults. The other agent is not cited because it has no data-processing controls to compare.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into oh-my-openagent
IF retention or telemetry is enabled for that session
mitigations: Avoid entering regulated data into the pair
Disable telemetry where possible
Clear session history after use
Separate compliant and non-compliant workflows
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
